text:
A third-round pick who spent part of 2020-21 in the ECHL, Tommy Novak has become one of Pittsburgh's most productive forwards at a fraction of the stars' ice time. He has 15 points (8 goals) in 21 games while playing 15.6 minutes, and our wins added, which credits goals at the moments they swing games, ranks him 40th of 548 skaters.

The process is good. The Penguins take 55.4% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, 3.6 points better than without him, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season (96th percentile among forwards once teammates and opponents are accounted for). His own expected goals are up on last season's rate too, and his ice time has grown by about a minute over his last ten games.

The finishing is ahead of itself. He is shooting 21.1%, above the top of our range for him, with one of the softer shots in the league (14th percentile for top speed), and Pittsburgh has scored 4.4 more goals than its chances deserved with him on. Our range for his season is 44 to 65 points; what we'd watch is whether the bigger minutes stick.
